input_contract.description: A string of 1-100 lowercase letters and a round count k between 1 and 10. Order-sensitive because the positions are concatenated, not added.

mutants.description: adds the alphabet positions instead of concatenating them
performs one digit-summing round regardless of k
sums digits until one digit remains, ignoring k
operator swap: max of the digits instead of sum
loop bound short by one: s[:-1]
EQUIVALENT: sums digits off the string without the int round trip
mutants.equivalence_argument: The reference computes int(text) and then sums its decimal digits. No alphabet position is 0, so text has no leading zero and int(text) round-trips to exactly text — the digit multiset is identical. Summing the digits of text directly therefore produces the same first-round value, and the remaining k-1 rounds are identical. Equal on every input in the specification's range.

t1-alphabet-is-zero-based.why_wrong: The specification says a is 1 and z is 26. A learner reaching for ord(c) - ord('a') gets a zero-based alphabet, which is the standard Python idiom and wrong here.

t1-digital-root-instead-of-k-rounds.why_wrong: 'Repeatedly replace by the digit sum' reads as the digital root to anyone who has met that idea before. It agrees with the reference whenever k is large enough to reach a fixed point, so it hides behind most tests.

t1-rounds-run-k-minus-one-times.why_wrong: Counting the conversion itself as the first round is a natural off-by-one when the problem describes 'transform, then repeat'.

t1-single-round-ignores-k.why_wrong: The specification says the round runs exactly k times, no more and no fewer. A learner who reads 'sum the digits' as a single step ignores k entirely, and every k=1 test still passes.

t1-sums-positions-instead-of-concatenati.why_wrong: The specification's load-bearing sentence is that the conversion CONCATENATES positions rather than adding them. Adding is the more natural reading of 'convert the letters to numbers' and is the single likeliest misreading of this problem.
